findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed eggs to be stored above cupcakes in cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage order and eggs were relocated to bottom of cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mop to be stored in bottom mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper mop storage and mop was moved to mop strainer. Ensure mop is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed a food handling employee to come to the kitchen and wash hands appropriately; however, a barrier was not used to turn off the faucet handles (prevents against cross contamination). Discussed with employee. Employee re-washed hands correctly. PIC/CFPM washed hands correctly multiple times. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no active sani buckets upon start of inspection. PIC/CFPM was actively making cookies during inspection. Ensure a sanitization bucket is made prior to starting food preparation. Discussed with PIC/CFPM. PIC made a sani spray bottle of quaternary ammonium. Test strips were readily available to check concentrations. Ensure paper towel use with spray bottles of sanitizer (not in-use rags; rags can be used in sanitization buckets as long as they are immersed in sanitizer in between uses). COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Milk and heavy whipping cream are observed in the standing cooler without date marking. PIC stated that they were penned a week ago today. A conversation took place in relation to 7 day date marking requirements and it was suggested to purchase smaller containers of these products (as the facility does not use them often). The items were discarded during the inspection to correct.
